questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay for other drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with a single rider.
You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
A motorcycle's brake lights will turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane. Before passing a motorcycle on the left, make sure your entire vehicle is in the left lane.

questions.question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, you should:

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you start driving.
Only have a general idea of where you are going.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Plan your trip in advance before driving to an unfamiliar area. Do not start with only a vague idea of your destination. Check a map to find the location before you drive.

questions.question: Which is NOT a factor in how far your vehicle takes to stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. This sign warns drivers to be extra careful when the road is wet because it may be slippery and harder to control.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use light braking.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by taking your foot off the gas and using light braking.

questions.question: To turn quickly, your hands should be:

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely at high speeds.

questions.question: If someone is following you too closely on a two-lane road:

options.text: Slowly reduce your speed to let them pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Tap your brakes to slow down, then resume your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly reduce your speed to let them pass you.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, try to move to a different lane. If you cannot change lanes, slowly reduce your speed to encourage them to pass you.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use your high beam headlights.
questions.correctAnswerText: FALSE
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams can reflect off the fog and shine back into your eyes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings and prepare drivers for upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: The maximum speed limit in rural areas is ____, unless federal law allows a higher speed.
questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit in rural areas is 55 mph, unless federal law allows higher. In cities and residential areas, the maximum is 30 mph.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other:

options.text: It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing the tracks.
When one train passes, check the other track before proceeding.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When one train passes, check the other track before proceeding.
questions.explanation: When two railroad tracks are next to each other, watch for a second train after one passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming on either track.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, you should not:

options.text: Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: If hit from behind, keep your seat belt on. Brace yourself by pressing against the back of your seat and put your head against the head restraint. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake.

questions.question: You see a steady yellow traffic light ahead. If you have not entered the intersection yet, you should:

options.text: Speed up to beat the red light.
Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means prepare to stop. If you are already in the intersection, drive through quickly.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb:

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn your wheels sharply away from the curb. This keeps your car from rolling into traffic. On streets with no curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road instead.

questions.question: Ramps and bridges freeze before regular highways and roads.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Ramps and bridges freeze faster than regular roads because they are in the air. Drive slowly and carefully when crossing bridges in cold weather.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the wheels toward the curb.
Turn the wheels away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb toward the center of the street. The back of the tire should rest against the curb.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first:

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of your parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of your parking space.
questions.explanation: First, find a parking space and check traffic. Signal, then stop parallel to the car in front of your desired space. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: You should signal 50 to 75 feet before turning at an intersection.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: In South Carolina, you must signal at least 100 feet before making any turn.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow on a traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Merge in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn left after checking for oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Turn because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow means a red arrow is about to appear. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You are driving in the wrong direction.
Treat it like a stop sign.
Wait until the light turns green before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works the same as a stop sign. Stop completely at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Let all other cars and pedestrians pass before you go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill or downgrade is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill or downgrade is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a steep or long hill ahead. The hill may have sharp curves too.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not brake if your car is skidding. Keep steering until your car is under control and moving safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: U-turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go the opposite direction where this sign is posted.

questions.question: What color are road markings that separate traffic going in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: When you see a flashing red light at an intersection, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, let other cars and pedestrians go, then proceed.
Stop and stay stopped as long as the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let other cars and pedestrians go, then proceed.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: A driver license is a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege, not a right.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn it and keep it.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers let you through.
Drive around the back of a car blocking you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If a car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a road with no curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn your wheels toward the road edge.
Turn your wheels away from the road edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels toward the road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the road edge. This keeps your car from rolling onto the road if the brakes fail.

questions.question: How do you avoid glare from headlights of a car coming toward you?

options.text: Look briefly at the right side of the road.
Keep looking at the center line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly at the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights. Then check the position of the other car and keep looking ahead.
